findings.title: Missing double-check after acquiring write lock allows thundering herd
findings.body:
After releasing the RLock (line 43) and before acquiring the write Lock (line 48), another goroutine may have already populated `entryPointAssetsCache`. When multiple goroutines all observe a nil cache during the RLock phase (e.g., at startup), they all proceed to acquire the write lock and each one redundantly recomputes the value (file I/O or HTTP request) sequentially. The standard double-checked locking pattern requires re-checking the cache after acquiring the exclusive lock:

```go
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()
defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()
if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil {
    return entryPointAssetsCache, nil
}
```

Without this, N concurrent requests at startup will perform N redundant manifest reads instead of 1.
